summary: 53-foot steel live-in tower on Spokane Indian Reservation land, built 1975, staffed each summer, registered on the NHLR in 2018.

facts.design: 53-foot all-steel tower with a live-in cab

access.note: Administered by the Spokane Indian Reservation. No page read states a visitor rule; this level is carried over from our record and needs confirming with the reservation.

visit.trail_note: Paved West End Road, then gravel Sand Creek Road for about 6.5 miles to the summit. Sources say conditions vary with season and recent rain, but most cars should be able to make it.

events.note: 53-foot steel live-in tower, described as the first tower at the site
Date registered on the National Historic Lookout Register
Still staffed each fire season, per TrailChick (page last updated March 2024)

evidence.supports: Built 1975; 53-foot steel live-in tower; staffed every summer; first tower at this site
evidence.quote: Located in the Spokane Indian Reservation, this is 53-foot steel live-in tower was built in 1975. It is staffed every summer. It is the first tower at this site.

evidence.supports: Registered on the NHLR on October 6, 2018

evidence.supports: Built 1975 and the first tower on the site
evidence.quote: Built in 1975, this is the first tower ever built on the site.

evidence.supports: Built in 1975 as a 53-foot steel tower
evidence.quote: was built in 1975 and is one of the newer fire lookouts in Washington State.

evidence.supports: Route from the paved West End Road northeast of Fort Spokane

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 4,011 ft (1,223 m) and TrailChick and Willhite give about 4,000 ft. The difference is rounding; the story does not give an elevation.
Route signs say Lookout Mountain, but the tower and the register say Tower Mountain. The register and the tower sign are followed here.

sources.title: Tower Mountain Lookout - Spokane Indian Reservation

notes_for_editor: Build year, height, staffing and NHLR registration agree across four or more sources. The record's access level 'permission' is not stated by any page I read; check with the reservation before publishing that level. No notable fires or design history turned up in the sources reached, so the story is short. A Cheryl Hill search result for a Tower Mountain was an Oregon lookout (92-foot Aermotor tower, 1935) and was excluded.
